description: List every Bible translation this server holds and can quote word for word: the King James Version, modern English (Berean Standard Bible, World English Bible, ASV, YLT), the Catholic Douay-Rheims with the deuterocanonical books, Brenton's English Septuagint, about fifty other languages (Spanish, Portuguese, French, German, Chinese, Arabic, Hindi, Swahili, Russian, Korean and more), and the original Hebrew and Greek. Use it to find the translation id to pass as translation to scripture_passage, scripture_context, scripture_search, cross_references, verses_for, daily_bread or compare_translations, or to answer "which Bibles do you have", "can you quote the Bible in Spanish", "do you have the Catholic Bible". Not for reading a passage (scripture_passage), comparing one verse across Bibles (compare_translations), or the Hebrew or Greek words of a verse (original_words). language filters to one language (base subtag, so "pt-BR" matches "pt"); include_license_text adds each full license statement. Returns one row per translation with id, name, language, license copied verbatim from its source, canon and books held, versification and corpus hash, plus language_default (which id a language parameter picks) and excluded (translations deliberately left out and why). Deterministic, no network; a language with nothing held returns count 0 with empty true and the held languages listed. Access: no sign-in; shared limit of 300 requests a minute per IP.

include_license_text.description: True returns each license statement in full; false returns the short license and its source.

language.description: Optional BCP-47 language to filter by, e.g. "es" or "zh".

name: list_translations

attribution.description: Credit line for the data: The Living Bread (living-bread.org).

content_layers.description: Which fields are Scripture and which are human interpretation or reflection.

count.description: Translations returned; 0 when the language filter matches none.

evidence.description: Present when Scripture was read: translation, canon, corpus version, attribution, and a SHA-256 per passage.

excluded.description: Translations deliberately not held, each with the reason (usually a license that forbids redistribution).

freshness.description: How current the answer is: kind (scheduled | recently_observed | verified_live | record), retrieved_at, available_now (true only when activity was verified live).

ids.description: Up to 25 ids found in this answer, for follow-up calls.

language_default.description: Which translation id a language parameter picks, keyed by language tag.

license.description: License URL of the returned data (CC BY 4.0 unless stated).

next_actions.description: Up to 4 links the person can open next.

ok.description: Always true on a successful answer (errors come back as isError, never here).

original_languages.description: Ids of the Hebrew (wlc) and Greek (byz, tr) texts and the lexicon, for original_words.

result_state.description: "empty" when nothing matched (count 0, no results); the text then says so plainly.

source_url.description: The first public web page this answer came from or points to.

translations.description: One row per translation: id to pass as translation, name, BCP-47 language and language_name, short license (license_statement in full when asked), source, canon and canon_coverage, versification, verse count, corpus_version hash, books held, and the web door.

versification.description: The versification schemes used and how they map to the KJV numbering.

visibility.description: "public" for shared data, "yours" for the signed-in believer's own data.

title: The Bible translations held
